STEP 1 - Scene: A bowl of sliced fresh strawberries, photographed from directly above (top-down view). No other dishes are in frame.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white bowl is about 15 cm in diameter (cereal-bowl size), so its area is 3.14 x (7.5)^2 ≈ 177 cm^2. Strawberries are roughly 2-3 cm across per half-slice, so the bowl is a reasonable reference.

STEP 3 - Items: Sliced/halved fresh strawberries, with a little juice visible.

STEP 4 - Area: The strawberries fill nearly the whole visible bowl opening, roughly 90% of the bowl area (about 160 cm^2).

STEP 5 - Volume: The pile is mounded a few centimetres deep at the centre, so an average height of about 4 cm gives a gross volume of 160 x 4 ≈ 640 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut fruit bulk density is about 0.6 g/ml. 640 x 0.6 ≈ 384 g. Rounding for the uneven pile, I estimate about 380 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Fresh strawberries are about 32 kcal per 100 g. 380 x 0.32 ≈ 122 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A bowl of about 380 g of strawberries (roughly two to three cups' worth of halved berries) is plausible for a full cereal-size bowl, and 120 kcal is consistent with that quantity of fruit.
